A header is extra information attached to a network message or file that helps systems understand how to process it.
heap concept
The heap is an area of computer memory that programs use to store data while they are running.
help desk organization
A help desk is a support team that assists users with technical or account problems.
help desks organization
Help desks are support teams that assist users with technical problems, account access, and service requests.

high severity concept
High severity means a security issue is considered serious and should usually be fixed quickly.

HKLM\Software\synapse\Config\SealedConfig concept
HKLM\Software\synapse\Config\SealedConfig is a Windows Registry path referenced as a place where an application may store protected configuration data.
also: SealedConfig
HKLM\Software\SynapseAgent\metrics_interval concept
HKLM\Software\SynapseAgent\metrics_interval is a Windows Registry value referenced as a setting for how often a SynapseAgent component reports metrics.

honeypots tool

hong-kong other
Hong Kong is a special administrative region of China often mentioned as a location in cyber or business reporting.

The host kernel is the core of the operating system running on the physical machine that manages hardware and system resources.
href protocol
href is an HTML attribute that tells a link which web address it should open.
HTTP protocol
HTTP is a common way for computers to send web requests and responses over a network.
HTTP POST request protocol
An HTTP POST request is a web request commonly used to send data, such as a form submission or API payload, to a server.
HTTP(S) protocol
HTTP(S) refers to the web protocols used by browsers and websites, with HTTPS adding encryption for safer communication.
HTTP/1.0 200 OK protocol
HTTP/1.0 200 OK is a web server response meaning a request succeeded using version 1.0 of the HTTP protocol.

Human trafficking is the crime of exploiting people through force, fraud, or coercion for labor, services, or sex.
human trafficking victims concept
Human trafficking victims are people exploited through force, fraud, or coercion for labor, services, or sex trafficking.
Hunting technique
Hunting, often called threat hunting, means proactively searching for signs of attackers or suspicious activity instead of waiting for alerts.
IaC concept
Infrastructure as Code, the practice of managing and provisioning infrastructure through machine-readable configuration files.
iamlookingfor.org other
iamlookingfor.org is a web domain referenced in security reporting, such as a possible service location or indicator.
ICA Proxy tool
An ICA Proxy relays Citrix Independent Computing Architecture traffic so users can access remote apps or desktops.
ID cards concept
ID cards are documents or cards used to prove a person’s identity.
identities concept
Identities are accounts or actors that systems recognize and allow to access resources.
identity documents concept
Identity documents are official papers or digital records, such as passports or driver's licenses, used to prove who someone is.
identity security concept
Identity security is the practice of protecting user accounts, permissions, and login systems from misuse.
identity theft concept
Identity theft is when someone uses another person’s personal information without permission, often to commit fraud.
identity verification concept
Identity verification is the process of checking that someone is who they claim to be.
identity verification company organization
An identity verification company helps businesses check whether a person is who they claim to be.

IDScan organization
IDScan is an identity verification company or product name used for checking identity documents.
also: IDScan's

To impersonate trusted entities means pretending to be a legitimate person, company, or service to trick victims.

in memory concept
In memory means something runs or exists in a computer’s temporary working memory rather than as a normal file on disk.
In the wild concept
In the wild means a security flaw or attack is being used on real targets, not just tested in a lab.
Incident concept
A security incident is an event that may harm systems, data, or users and needs investigation or response.
incident log concept
An incident log is a record of what happened during a security incident and how it was handled.

pgoutput is PostgreSQL's built-in logical replication output plugin for sending database changes to subscribers.
Phish concept
Phish is a label for a deceptive message designed to trick a recipient.
phishing technique
Phishing is a scam where attackers impersonate trusted people or services to steal information or make victims take unsafe actions.

phishing campaign technique
A phishing campaign is a coordinated effort to trick people into giving up passwords, money, or other sensitive information.

phishing emails technique

phishing lures technique
Phishing lures are deceptive messages or pages designed to trick people into clicking, logging in, or opening something harmful.
PHP file concept

pivot technique
A pivot is an investigative move where one clue is used to find another related clue, such as moving from a domain to linked IP addresses.
pivoting technique
Pivoting is when an attacker uses one compromised system as a stepping stone to reach other systems or networks.
plaintext HTTP protocol
Plaintext HTTP is web traffic sent without encryption, meaning someone who can observe the connection may be able to read or modify it.

Plex Desktop is a desktop application for watching and managing Plex media on a computer.

plugin concept

plugins concept
Plugins are add-on pieces of software that extend what an application or website can do.
pod policies concept
Pod policies are Kubernetes rules that control what containerized workloads are allowed to do.
also: restricted pod policies, pod security settings
post-exploitation technique
Post-exploitation is what attackers do after breaking in, such as exploring systems, stealing data, or keeping access.
post-quantum cryptography concept
Post-quantum cryptography is encryption and digital signature technology designed to resist attacks from future quantum computers.

PostGREShell is a named PostgreSQL security issue or attack technique referenced in security reporting.
PostgreSQL product
PostgreSQL is a database system used to store and manage data.
also: PostgreSQL Project, PostgreSQL Global Development Group
PostgreSQL 14.24 product
PostgreSQL 14.24 is a specific release of the PostgreSQL open-source database system.
also: 14.24
PostgreSQL 15.19 product
PostgreSQL 15.19 is a specific release of the PostgreSQL open-source database system.
also: 15.19
PostgreSQL 16.15 product
PostgreSQL 16.15 is a specific release of the PostgreSQL open-source database system.
also: 16.15
PostgreSQL 17.11 product
PostgreSQL 17.11 is a specific release of the PostgreSQL open-source database system.
also: 17.11
PostgreSQL 18.6 product
PostgreSQL 18.6 is a specific release of the PostgreSQL open-source database system.
also: 18.6
PostgreSQL 9.4 product
PostgreSQL 9.4 is an older major release of the PostgreSQL open-source database system.
postgresshell tool
postgresshell is a tool or script name referenced in security reporting, likely related to interacting with PostgreSQL systems.
powershell
PowerShell is Microsoft’s command-line shell and scripting language, often used by administrators and abused by attackers.
PowerShell.exe tool
PowerShell.exe is the Windows program that opens PowerShell, a command-line shell often used for administration and sometimes abused by attackers.
Preparedness Framework concept
A Preparedness Framework is a structured plan for evaluating and reducing risks from advanced AI or other high-impact technologies.
President Donald Trump other
President Donald Trump is a U.S. political figure who served as the 45th president of the United States.
also: Trump
President Vladimir Putin other
President Vladimir Putin is the president of Russia.
also: Putin
PrettyPrague threat-actor
PrettyPrague is a named threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.
Previdian organization
Previdian is a named organization, product, or service referenced in security reporting.
Prince Group organization
Prince Group is a Cambodia-linked business group that authorities have associated with large-scale online scam operations and related criminal networks.
printable ASCII characters concept
Printable ASCII characters are basic visible text characters such as letters, numbers, punctuation, and spaces used by many computers.
also: ASCII characters
Prioritization concept
Prioritization means deciding which issues or tasks should be handled first based on importance or risk.
private industry partners organization
Private industry partners are non-government companies or organizations that work with another group on shared projects or security efforts.
private key concept
A private key is secret cryptographic data used to prove identity or decrypt information and must be kept confidential.
privilege-escalation technique
Privilege escalation is when an attacker gains higher levels of access than they were supposed to have.
privileged token concept
A privileged token is a digital credential that gives high-level access to systems or data.
privileged users concept
Privileged users are accounts or people with higher-than-normal access, such as administrators who can change important systems.
production concept
Production is the live environment where real users and real data are handled.
production systems concept
Production systems are the real live systems an organization uses to run its services or business.
prominent medical device company organization
A prominent medical device company is a well-known business that makes healthcare equipment and may be discussed as a cyber target or victim.
Prompt concept
A prompt is the instruction or question a person gives to an AI system to guide its response.
prompt injection technique
Prompt injection is a way of giving an AI system instructions that may make it behave in unintended ways.
also: indirect prompt injection
prompts concept
Prompts are the instructions or questions a user gives to an AI system to get a response.
proof-of-concept technique
A working demonstration, often a piece of code, that proves a security vulnerability can actually be exploited.
Proof-of-Concept Code concept
Proof-of-concept code is sample code that shows a security flaw can be exploited, often used by researchers and sometimes copied by attackers.
proof-of-concept exploit concept
A proof-of-concept exploit is sample code or a demonstration showing that a vulnerability can really be used.
also: PoC
Proof-of-concept exploit tool
A proof-of-concept exploit is sample code or a demonstration showing that a vulnerability can really be abused.
proof-of-concept exploits tool
Proof-of-concept exploits are example programs or instructions that show a security flaw can be used in practice.
proxy concept
A proxy is an intermediate server that forwards internet traffic between a user and a destination.
proxying technique
Proxying means routing internet traffic through another server or device so it appears to come from there instead of the original source.
public API concept
A public API is an interface that lets outside developers or systems interact with a service in a documented way.
Public exploit tool
A public exploit is code or instructions available to anyone that can take advantage of a known vulnerability.
public IP address concept
A public IP address is an internet-reachable network address that can be accessed from outside a private network.
public-key cryptography concept
Public-key cryptography is a way to secure messages using a pair of keys, one shared publicly and one kept private.
pull requests concept
Pull requests are proposals to merge code changes into a software project, commonly used on platforms like GitHub.
pull-request-target technique
pull-request-target is a GitHub Actions trigger that runs in the context of the target repository and can expose sensitive permissions if used carelessly.
Python tool
Python is a popular programming language often used to write scripts, automation tools, and security research code.
quantum computers concept
Quantum computers are computers that use quantum physics and may someday solve some problems much faster than normal computers.
quantum computing concept
Quantum computing is a type of computing that uses quantum physics and could one day solve some problems much faster than today’s computers.
Quantum cyber threats concept
Quantum cyber threats are future cybersecurity risks from quantum computers that could break some encryption methods used today.
also: quantum threat, quantum-related cyber threats
Quantum technologies concept
Quantum technologies use the physics of very small particles and may affect computing, encryption, and communications.
Quantum-resistant technology concept
Quantum-resistant technology is designed to stay secure even against future quantum computers.
also: quantum-resistant cryptography
quarantined concept
Quarantined means a suspicious file, email, or system has been isolated so it cannot easily cause harm while it is investigated.
quarterly compliance updates concept
Quarterly compliance updates are security or regulatory status reports provided every three months.
ransomware concept
Ransomware is malicious software or an operation that locks or steals data to pressure victims into paying money.
also: ransomware attacks, ransomware incidents, ransomware-related data breaches, custom ransomware strain
ransomware gangs threat-actor
Criminal groups that use malicious software to encrypt victims' data and demand payment for its release.
ransomware reporting concept
Ransomware reporting is the process of notifying authorities, regulators, insurers, or stakeholders about a ransomware incident.
Rapid7 organization
A security firm providing vulnerability management, orchestration, and incident detection products like InsightVM and Metasploit.
Rapid7 Labs organization
Rapid7 Labs is Rapid7’s research team that analyzes vulnerabilities, threats, and internet-scale security data.
RDP Proxy tool
An RDP Proxy is a server that relays Remote Desktop Protocol connections between a user and a remote computer.
reachability concept
Reachability means whether one system, account, or network location can access another.
reachability analysis technique
Reachability analysis checks whether a vulnerable or risky piece of code can actually be reached and triggered in a real application.
reactive detection concept
Reactive detection means finding threats after suspicious activity or damage has already happened.
also: Reactive security
README concept
A README is a text file that explains what a project or folder is and how to use it.
Real time concept
Real time means something happens or is shown immediately, or with very little delay.
also: live stream, live access
Reasoning concept
Reasoning is the process of working through information logically to reach an answer or decision.
Reboot concept
A reboot means restarting a computer, phone, server, or other device.
recommendation concept
A recommendation is suggested guidance or an action that someone should consider taking to reduce risk or solve a problem.
Red Hat organization
Red Hat is a technology company known for enterprise Linux and related software.
regex concept
Regex, short for regular expression, is a pattern used to search for or match specific text.
Registry concept
The Registry is a Windows database that stores system and application settings.
regular expressions concept
Regular expressions are special text patterns used to search for or match strings such as emails, keys, or file names.
regulator concept
A regulator is an organization that oversees and enforces rules in a specific area.
relayed concept
Relayed means traffic or messages are passed through another system instead of going directly from sender to receiver.
remediated concept
Remediated means a security issue has been fixed or otherwise addressed.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.
also: remediation deadline, remediation time
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.

Remote access tools let someone control or manage a computer from another location, which can be legitimate or abused by attackers.
also: remote access tool
remote access trojan malware
A remote access trojan is malware that secretly lets an attacker control a victim's computer from somewhere else.
also: RAT
remote attacker concept
A remote attacker is someone who tries to exploit a system over a network without needing physical access to it.
remote commands concept
Remote commands are instructions sent over a network to make another computer or device do something.
Remote Desktop concept
A technology that lets you see and control a computer's desktop from another device over a network.
remote desktop passkey phishing technique
Remote desktop passkey phishing is an attack that uses remote access sessions to trick a victim into approving a passkey sign-in.
Remote management concept
Remote management is controlling or configuring a computer, server, or device from another location over a network.
Remote shell tool
A remote shell is command-line access to a computer over a network.
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
Remotely tool
Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
REPLICATION attribute concept
The REPLICATION attribute is a PostgreSQL role permission that allows a user to perform replication-related actions.
also: REPLICATION
replication protocol protocol
A replication protocol is the set of rules a database uses to send copied data or change records to another system.
Report Fraud product
Report Fraud is a public service or portal name used for submitting fraud reports to authorities or organizations.
also: national service, new platform
repositories concept
Repositories are places where software project files and related development data are stored.
reputation-based filtering technique
Reputation-based filtering blocks or allows emails, websites, or files based on whether they are known to be trustworthy or suspicious.
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
resilience concept
The ability of an organization to anticipate, withstand, and recover from adverse cyber events and security breaches.
Restart concept
A restart is turning a device or program off and then back on again to refresh it or apply changes.
Reuters organization
Reuters is an international news organization that reports on business, politics, technology, and security events.
reverse network tunnels technique
Reverse network tunnels are connections initiated from inside a network back to an outside system to carry traffic through restricted boundaries.
reverse proxy connections technique
Reverse proxy connections are network connections where an intermediary server receives requests and forwards them to backend systems.

A Reverse SOCKS5 proxy lets traffic be relayed through a remote machine back to an attacker or operator, often to reach otherwise hidden systems.
also: SOCKS5 listener, SOCKS5 traffic
RFC 9989 protocol
RFC 9989 is a numbered internet standards document that describes a technical specification or protocol behavior.

Ricochet Chollima is a named threat actor group referenced in security reporting, likely associated with North Korean activity.
Roadmap concept
A roadmap is a plan showing future work, releases, or security improvements over time.
romance concept
Romance refers to romantic relationships or dating contexts, which criminals may exploit in romance scams to manipulate victims.
romance fraud concept
Romance fraud is a scam where someone pretends to have a romantic relationship to gain trust and steal money or information.
root access concept
Having complete administrative control over a computer or network, allowing unrestricted system changes.
also: root, local root escalation, root escalation
root cause concept
Root cause means the underlying reason a problem or security incident happened, not just its visible symptoms.
Rosneft organization
Rosneft is a major Russian oil and gas company that may be relevant in infrastructure or geopolitical security reporting.
also: Russian oil giant Rosneft
Ruby tool
Ruby is a programming language used to build software and web applications.
run code concept
To run code means to make a computer execute instructions written in a programming language.
runtime concept
Runtime is the period when a program is actively running, or the software environment it needs in order to run.

russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
Russian government organization
The Russian government is Russia's national governing organization and is often mentioned in cyber and geopolitical reporting.
Russian media organization
Russian media refers to news and information outlets based in or focused on Russia.
RUVDS organization
RUVDS is a hosting and virtual server provider referenced in security reporting.

RxRPC is a network protocol used by the Linux kernel and AFS to support remote procedure calls.
Ryan Dewhurst other
Ryan Dewhurst is a security researcher known for work related to web application security tools and research.
also: Dewhurst
SafeChain product
SafeChain is a named product, tool, or organization referenced in security reporting.
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.
SAFER product
SAFER is a U.S. motor-carrier information system run by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.
Salvatore Gulizia other
Salvatore Gulizia is a named individual referenced in security reporting.

SAMA Cybersecurity Framework concept
The SAMA Cybersecurity Framework is a Saudi Central Bank cybersecurity framework for financial organizations.
also: SAMA CSF

SAML is a standard that lets users sign in once and access multiple services by passing trusted identity messages between them.

SAML Action is a field or element in the SAML authentication standard that can describe an action a user is allowed to perform.
sanctioned concept
Sanctioned means officially restricted or penalized by a government, often by banning business dealings or freezing assets.
sanctions concept
Government-imposed restrictions that block or limit trade, financial dealings, or travel with targeted individuals or countries.
sandbag tool
Sandbag is a named tool, project, or technique referenced in security reporting.
also: sandbag covertly
sandbox concept
A sandbox is an isolated environment used to run code more safely so it cannot easily affect the rest of the system.

A sandboxed renderer process is a restricted browser component that displays web pages while limiting damage if malicious code runs.

SBOMs, or software bills of materials, are lists of the components and dependencies used inside a software product.

SCA concept

Scam technique
A scam is a dishonest scheme designed to trick people into giving up money, information, or access.
Scam Center Strike Force organization
Scam Center Strike Force is an organization or law-enforcement initiative referenced in reporting about combating scam operations.
scam centers organization
Scam centers are organized workplaces where criminals run fraud schemes, often using phones, messaging apps, or fake websites.

scam compounds concept
Scam compounds are physical locations where organized groups run large-scale online fraud operations, often using coerced labor.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
scanner tool
A scanner is a tool that searches for information or problems automatically.
Scanners tool
Scanners are tools that check systems, networks, or websites for exposed services, weaknesses, or signs of compromise.
scanning technique
Scanning is checking computers, networks, or services to find what is reachable and what may be vulnerable.
scans concept
Scans are automated checks that examine software or related data for issues or information.
schema concept
A schema is a defined structure that describes how data should be organized and what fields it should contain.
scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.

Scoring is the practice of assigning a number or rating to show how risky, important, or suspicious something is.
seccomp
seccomp is a Linux security feature that restricts which system calls a program can make.

security data concept
Security data is information such as logs, alerts, and network records used to detect and investigate threats.
also: data
Security fixes concept
Security fixes are software updates that repair weaknesses attackers could exploit.
Security incidents concept
Security incidents are events that threaten the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of systems or data.
security professionals concept
Security professionals are people whose job is to protect systems, data, and organizations from security threats.
security software product
Security software is software designed to protect computers, networks, or data from threats.
security teams concept
Groups of professionals responsible for protecting an organization's information, systems, and networks from cyber threats.

security updates concept
Security updates are software fixes that close vulnerabilities or improve protection against threats.

Sender domains are the internet domain names used to send emails, such as the part after the @ sign.
sensitive data concept
Sensitive data is information that could cause harm if exposed, such as passwords, financial details, or medical records.
sensitive information concept
Sensitive information is data that should be protected because exposing it could harm a person, company, or system.

Sensitive personal information is private data, such as identity, health, financial, or contact details, that could harm someone if exposed.
sensors tool
Devices or software components that collect data or monitor activity for analysis.
Sentinel product
Sentinel is a security product name referenced in security reporting, often associated with monitoring and threat detection.

Service delays and failures are disruptions that make an online service slow, unreliable, or unavailable.

Service logs are records created by software or cloud services that show what actions or errors occurred.
service providers organization

severity concept
Severity is a rating that describes how serious a security issue is.

also: Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver
Shahid Hemmat organization
Shahid Hemmat is an Iranian organization or entity referenced in security and sanctions reporting.
Shahid Shushtari organization
Shahid Shushtari is an Iranian organization or entity referenced in security and sanctions reporting.
sharepoint
SharePoint is Microsoft’s platform for storing, sharing, and collaborating on documents and internal websites.
shell commands concept
Shell commands are text instructions typed into a command line to tell a computer what to do.
shipping concept
Shipping is the industry that moves goods by sea, air, road, or rail and can be a target in cyber incidents.
SideCopy threat-actor
SideCopy is a threat-actor group referenced in security reporting, often associated with espionage activity in South Asia.
also: Pakistan-linked SideCopy group

A security tool that gathers and analyzes logs from across an organization in real time to spot suspicious activity.
siloed tools concept
Siloed tools are separate systems that do not share information well with each other.
Simulations concept
Simulations are practice scenarios that imitate real events so people or systems can test how they would respond.
SLA concept
An SLA, or service-level agreement, is a promise about how quickly or reliably a service will be delivered.

slack

SLAs, or service-level agreements, are promises about the level of service a provider will deliver, such as uptime or response time.
Small and medium-sized businesses organization
Small and medium-sized businesses are companies that are smaller than large enterprises and often have fewer security resources.

SOC organization

social media concept
Social media means online platforms where people share messages, photos, videos, and other content.

SOCs, or Security Operations Centers, are teams and facilities that monitor, investigate, and respond to cybersecurity threats.
software concept
Software is the programs and apps that tell computers and devices what to do.

Software flaws are mistakes or weaknesses in programs that can cause bugs or create security risks.
software vulnerabilities vulnerability
Software vulnerabilities are weaknesses in programs that attackers may use to gain access, steal data, or disrupt systems.

south-africa other
South Africa is a country that may be mentioned as a location or target in a security story.
south-korea

southeast-asia other

spearphishing technique

specterops organization

splice() technique

sqlite

suppliers organization

suspicious activity concept

technology platforms product

ted tool
